newsitem.title: GERMANY: IWH - Germany unlikely to meet 3.0 percent EMU goal.
newsitem.headline: IWH - Germany unlikely to meet 3.0 percent EMU goal.

text.p: Germany is unlikely to meet the 3.0 percent deficit goal for European currency union membership, Ruediger Pohl, President of the Halle Economic Research Institute (IWH), said on Friday.

"Based on the current trends, I find 3.0 percent hard to imagine," Pohl told Reuters in an interview. He was referring to the Maastricht criterion which requires would-be currency union members to have budget deficits of three percent of gross domestic product (GDP).
However, the IWH chief said that 3.4 percent would not pose a problem for European economic and monetary union (EMU).
"I must add, that I think that 3.4 percent would pose no problem for currency union," Pohl said.

The institute's president said there was a mistake in the way government is looking at the deficit criteria, because there would only be a direct relationship between the deficit and monetary union if the future European Central Bank (ECB) could print money to finance deficits.
Because this is not allowed, the deficit criterion was not critical for monetary union, he said.
Pohl criticised the single currency debate in Germany.
"In Germany, we have an irrational, emotional discussion which is not objective."
He also said that the discussion about Germany's budgetary difficulties and planned tax reforms was hindering investment in the country.

"The budget discussions are sparking uncertainty," he said, adding that investors were nervous about the lack of clarity of how much reform would be possible and to what extent reform would be blocked by the opposition-controlled upper house.
